intended_object: This is the braiding morphism M ⊗ N → N ⊗ M in the matrix envelope Mat_ C of a braided monoidal preadditive category C. It is the matrix that has the component braiding β_{M_{i}, N_{j}} at entry ((i,j),(j,i)) and 0 everywhere else, so it is the braiding of C reindexed by the swap M.ι × N.ι ≃ N.ι × M.ι. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation, and it is used as `braiding` in the `BraidedCategory (Mat_ C)` instance.
explanation:
In this library the tensor product in Mat_ C is defined as follows:
- (M ⊗ N).ι = M.ι × N.ι, with (M ⊗ N).X (i,j) = M.X i ⊗ N.X j;
- the tensor product of morphisms is the Kronecker product.

A morphism (M ⊗ N) ⟶ (N ⊗ M) is therefore a family of components M.X i₁ ⊗ N.X i₂ ⟶ N.X j₁ ⊗ M.X j₂. The definition takes the component to be nonzero exactly when i₂ = j₁ and i₁ = j₂. In that case it is the braiding β_{M.X j₂, N.X j₁}, composed first with the `eqToHom` that rewrites the source along these index equalities. Every other component is 0.

This is the standard braiding on the additive (matrix) envelope: a permutation matrix for the swap of index sets, with braidings of C as entries. The same file proves that it is an isomorphism, that it is natural, and that it satisfies both hexagon identities. It also proves that it gives a symmetric structure when C is symmetric.

The generality is natural. It uses only a preadditive braided monoidal C and the existing Mathlib construction `Mat_ C`. Mathlib has no monoidal or braided structure on `Mat_`: there is no match for `Monoidal` or `Braid` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Preadditive/Mat.lean`. So there is no Mathlib counterpart, and the definition does not re-implement anything Mathlib provides.
